criteria.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-cli: a test calling drain() with a priority record that lowers an urgent-text request shows that item is started after a higher-priority item. It covers both a record present before drain() starts and one added while an earlier item runs.
criteria.evidence: Both tests passed. They call `drain::drain` on a real Fixture with real queue, plan and priority records; only run and land are faked, in the `Replay` wrapper. They assert `started == [u1, n, u2]` with the low record committed before drain starts and, through the `on_run` hook, while U1 runs. On base code the mid-run case would start U2 second, because base built the plan once at the start.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a test builds one queue and shows the sequence of jobs drain() starts equals the entries athena plan's plan() returns for the same queue, including a group-1 item that has a cited-but-not-'Depends on' job id.
criteria.evidence: `drain_order_equals_plan_order` passed. It asserts that `plan.groups[0][0]` is the request citing the refused job id outside a 'Depends on' line, that `started == planned.plan.order`, and that the refused item gets exactly one 'plan       … passed over' line with 'the plan lacks acceptance'. `drain_order_follows_the_plan_as_the_queue_changes` also passed: after an urgent request is queued mid-run, the drain's later dispatches equal the order `drain::plan` printed at that moment.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-cli: a test shows each planned item that is not worked (held, refused, cyclic, not ready, clash with a running batch, over budget, job limit, run ended first) gets exactly one UI log line with its job id and a reason, once per run.
criteria.evidence: `passed_over_item_is_logged_once_with_its_reason` passed. It covers refused, held, cyclic, not ready, job limit, budget, stop requested/run ended first and a shared-path clash, and asserts exactly one 'plan       <id> passed over: ' line holding the reason in each case. It also checks that no line appears when every item is worked. `a_replan_does_not_read_an_underspecified_item_twice` passed: one read and one 'is underspecified' line across waves. The clash scenario runs on the serial drain only, not `drain_concurrent` (see findings).

criteria.criterion: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test: all pass, and the existing drain tests pass unchanged.
criteria.evidence: Athena's records for this tree: fmt passed, clippy passed, `cargo test --locked` passed (1761 tests). `git diff HEAD~1 -- crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs` shows only additions: two new defaulted fields and branches on `Stub`, plus new tests and helpers. No existing test body was edited.

criteria.criterion: Grep of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs and crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs shows drain takes its order from the same plan-building code as plan(), with no separate ordering in drain.
criteria.evidence: Grep tool: in drain.rs, `Plan::build_with` is called only at line 1661 inside `fn prepare`, which both `plan()` (line 2461) and `drain_with` call. `Plan::build` appears only in tests. The two `sort_by_key` calls (1573, 2288) are the `place` age sorts that feed `build_with`. The old inline batch building was removed; `batches_for` filters `plan.groups` without reordering. Its unit test passed: the flattened batches equal `plan.order`, and `tried` removes only the tried items.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry that names the cause found, the order fix and the passed-over log line.
criteria.evidence: The new Unreleased 'Fixed' entry names the cause: a plan built once and frozen, with skips going only to notes. It also names two weighed alternatives: proposal approval, and an old binary that treated a cited job id as a dependency. It states the fix (re-plan after each wave through `Drain::prepare` and `Plan::build_with`, with `batches_for` only filtering) and the line `plan       <id> passed over: <reason>`.

findings.summary: The clash reason is tested only on the serial drain, and there it can name an item that never ran.
findings.evidence: The clash case uses `Stub` with `drain::drain` (serial), not `drain_concurrent` as planned. The test expects c's line to say 'shares src/x.rs with b, so it was waiting for it', yet b itself was passed over with 'stop requested' and never ran. In serial mode every item waits for the one before it anyway, so the 'waiting for it' wording can mislead.

findings.summary: The drain report still shows the first plan's groups and refusals, while its queued list comes from the last plan.
findings.evidence: `plan_groups: plan.groups, refused: plan.refused` use `first_plan`, while `queued` uses the last re-planned `view`. After a mid-run re-plan, the report's plan groups can differ from what was worked. This is probably kept for existing tests, but it is a small inconsistency for a reader comparing the drain with `athena plan`.

findings.summary: Proposal approval is named as a possible cause of divergence but left as is.
findings.evidence: The entry says the drain approves in-limit proposals that `athena plan` never shows. The approved items are ordered by the same plan builder, so this is a difference in which items are listed, not in how they are ordered. Naming it is reasonable.

summary: The change fixes the drain so it works items in the order `athena plan` prints. The cause it found is that the drain built its plan once, at the start, and then worked that frozen list. A priority record, a job end or a request queued after the start never reached it. Now, after each item (or each group under `drain_concurrent`), the drain reads the queue again and rebuilds the plan through the same `Drain::prepare` and `Plan::build_with` that `plan()` uses. `batches_for` only drops items already tried; it never reorders. Readings, approvals and refusals are carried across plans, so nothing is read or paid for twice. Each planned item that is not worked gets one `plan       <id> passed over: <reason>` line per run. I ran all the new targeted tests and they pass: both priority-record tests (record committed before the start and while an item runs), both drain-order tests (including a group-1 item that cites a job id outside a 'Depends on' line), the passed-over scenario table, the read-once replan test, the `batches_for` unit test and the `shared_path` test. Athena's fmt, clippy and test records all passed. The existing tests in tests/drain.rs were not edited; the diff only adds tests and two defaulted fields to `Stub`. Grep finds no second ordering in drain.rs. The CHANGELOG entry names the cause, the fix and the log line. The only findings are minor: the clash reason is tested only on the serial drain and can name an item that never ran, and the report still shows the first plan.
